by 1,3-Dipolar Cycloadditions of Nitrones with
Allenylphosphonates
Rayhane Hammami, Lucas Mele, Soufiane Touil, David Virieux, Jean-François Poisson,*

A general and effective (3  2) cycloaddition reaction between
nitrones and allenes to synthesize fluoro-phosphonopyrrolidin-

1. Introduction
Nitrogen-containing heterocycles are widely present in biologically

were thus selected as potential candidates. To the best of our
knowledge, no example of such reagent has been reported in
the literature. Fluorinated allenylphosphonates 2 were synthesized

chlorophosphite was synthesized according to a procedure
described in the literature,<sup>[11]</sup> by reacting phosphorus trichloride
with trifluoroethanol in the presence of N,N-diethylaniline as a
base. The resulting chlorophosphite was then reacted with three
different propargyl alcohols

yielding the corresponding

With these fluorinated allenylphosphonates 2a–c in hand, we
decided to explore their reactions with nitrones. Initially, we
evaluated the cycloaddition of (Z)-N-methyl-phenylnitrone with
allene 2a using the optimal conditions developed in our prece-
dent report.<sup>[9]</sup> While the diethyl phosphonate analog delivered
the expected product in only 34% yield,<sup>[12]</sup> the use of fluori-
nated allenylphosphonate 2a resulted in a significantly improved
78% isolated yield of the pyrrolidine-3-one 3a (Scheme 3).
Noteworthy, the reaction exhibited a complete regio- and stereo-
selectivity, 3a being formed exclusively as the
-trans isomer.
Encouraged by the improved reactivity, reactions of allenyl-
phosphonates 2a–c were then explored under these conditions.
Nitrones bearing different aromatic substituents were first-
tested with allene 2a. The reaction proceeded smoothly with
complete diastereoselectivity, yielding only the trans-products
in moderate to good yields. The presence of -electron-donating-
or withdrawing groups in the para or meta position (3b–3f) of the
aromatic moiety has little influence on the reaction outcome.
However, the yield decreased when the phenyl group of the
nitrone was replaced by a furyl group (3g). It has also been pos-
sible to replace the N-methyl group of the nitrone by N-benzyl,
with a slight decrease in yield (78% for 3a vs. 66% for 3h).
The reaction of cyclic nitrone, 5,5-dimethyl-1-pyrroline-N-oxide
(DMPO) with the allene 2a successfully delivered the pyrrolidi-
none product 3j in 58% yield. We subsequently evaluated the
outcome of this transformation using racemic allenes 2b and
2c. Products 3k and 3l were also obtained with a complete C<sup>4</sup>,

Building on these positive outcomes, we investigated whether
this MW-assisted (3 2) cycloaddition involving nitrones could be
applied to allenylphosphonate 6 containing a basic piperidine
functional group. If successful, this approach could streamline
the synthesis of valuable new spirocyclic piperidinyl–pyrrolidinyl
phosphonates, offering an unprecedented scaffold. Indeed, many
spirocyclic piperidines have been developed as drugs or have
demonstrated highly promising activities in preclinical and clinical
studies. Notable examples include Fenspiride,<sup>[13]</sup> marketed as
Pneumorel, which acts as an alpha-1 blocker. Spiperone is a
selective
\mathsf { D } _ { 2 }
dopamine receptor antagonist,<sup>[14]</sup> and Liproxstatin-1
is a ferroptosis inhibitor which reduces iron deposition, thereby
alleviating renal fibrosis induced by unilateral ureteral obstruction
(Figure 2).<sup>[15]</sup> Therefore, as outlined in this study, the development
of phosphonate-based bioisosteres within this important class
of compounds holds particular promise. To the best of our

for 2 h in cyclohexane (1.0 M) under
MW irradiation), only 57% of the desired cycloaddition product
7h could be isolated (Scheme 6). The decrease in yield was
likely due to the formation of numerous by-products with similar
polarity to the desired spirocyclic pyrrolidin-3-one 7h, including
unreacted starting material 1g. To address this issue, we reinvesti-
gated some parameters of this MW-assisted (3 2) cycloaddition.
Gratifyingly, increasing the amount of nitrone 1g to 1.5 equiva-
lents significantly reduced the formation of polar by-products.
The chemical outcome of the reaction was further improved
by conducting the reaction under more diluted conditions
(0.2 vs. 1.0 M), extending the reaction time to 3 h, and replacing
cyclohexane with toluene, leading to the spirocyclic pyrrolidin-3-
one 7h with an optimal 74% yield.

Having established the optimized reaction conditions for the
MW-assisted (3 2) cycloaddition of nitrone 1g with piperidine-
substituted allenylphosphonate 6, we then investigated the
substrate scope. As shown in Scheme 6, with the exception of
the phenyl derivative, nitrones bearing either electron-donating
(methoxy) or electron-withdrawing functional groups (fluorine,
and bromine) performed well in this reaction, producing the
desired products 7a–i in moderate to good yields (47%–79%)
with a trans relative configuration. Interestingly, when substitu-
ents were present in the ortho-position of the aryl moiety, the
spirocyclic derivatives were obtained in good to high isolated
yields (7b,e,h 69%–79%), suggesting that steric hindrance had
a negligible impact on the reaction.
To evaluate the synthetic potential of phosphonopyrrolidinones
3 for further modifications, we evaluated their reactivity as Still–
Gennari olefination partners. In the presence of paraformaldehyde,
diisopropylethylamine (DIPEA) and LiCl, phosphonopyrrolidinone 3a
afforded the corresponding 4-methylydenepyrrolidin-3-one 8a (78%
yield, Scheme 7). While the reaction of the diphenylphosphinoxy
analog was efficient with paraformaldehyde,<sup>[9]</sup> it failed to deliver

Interestingly, when tested with the fluorinated phosphinylpyrroli-
din-3-one 3a, the reaction proceeded smoothly. Using benzalde-
hyde, the corresponding product 8b was obtained in 69% yield
as a Z:E (85:15) mixture of diastereoisomers. The transformation
was further extended to other aromatic and heteroaromatic alde-
hydes, and the expected products 8b–f were obtained in low to
good yields and average to excellent diastereoselectivities. The
Z-configuration of the major diastereoisomers was determined by
(NOESY) nuclear overhauser effect spectroscopy experiments.
In summary, we successfully synthesized two series of phos-
phonopyrrolidinones using a general and affordable approach
to introduce diastereoselectively structural diversity. The first series
demonstrated that bis(2,2,2-trifluoroethyl) allenylphosphonates
are effective reagents in the (3 2) cycloaddition with nitrones,
achieving moderate to good yields and good diastereoselectivity.
Pyrrolidinone 3a also showed good reactivity in the Still–Gennari
olefination leading to the vinylidene pyrrolidinones 8 even using
aromatic aldehydes. Additionally, we successfully applied this MW-
assisted (3 2) cycloaddition reaction with nitrones to piperidinyl
allenylphosphonate 6. This highly convergent reaction led in one
step to valuable and complex spirocyclic piperidinyl-pyrrolidin-3-
ones 7 in yields ranging from 33% to 79%. Further studies to
evaluate the biological properties of these new compounds are
currently underway and will be reported in due course.
2. Experimental Section
General procedure for synthesis of fluorinated phosphinylpyrro-
lidin-3-one 3: in a sealed tube, nitrone 1 (0.500 mmol), fluorinated
allenylphosphonates 2 (0.500 mmol), and cyclohexane (0.5 mL)
were heated at 150 °C under MW irradiation for 2 h. After the
completion of the reaction, the mixture was concentrated under
reduced pressure and the crude material was purified by column
chromatography over silica gel (pentane/EtOAc) to afford pure
fluorinated phosphonopyrrolidinones 3.
General procedure for synthesis of spirocyclic phosphonopyr-
rolidinones 7: in a 7 mL MW tube, nitrone 1 (0.600 mmol), diethyl
(2-(1-benzylpiperidin-4-ylidene)vinyl)phosphonate 6 (140 mg,
0.400 mmol), and toluene (2.0 mL) were heated at 150 °C under
MW irradiation for 3 h. After the completion of the reaction,
the mixture was concentrated under reduced pressure and
the crude material was purified by column chromatography
over silica gel (dichloromethane/MeOH 99:1 to 95:5) to afford
pure spirocyclic phosphonopyrrolidinones 7.

Having established the optimized reaction conditions for the
MW-assisted (3 2) cycloaddition of nitrone 1g with piperidine-
substituted allenylphosphonate 6, we then investigated the
substrate scope. As shown in Scheme 6, with the exception of
the phenyl derivative, nitrones bearing either electron-donating
(methoxy) or electron-withdrawing functional groups (fluorine,
and bromine) performed well in this reaction, producing the
desired products 7a–i in moderate to good yields (47%–79%)
with a trans relative configuration. Interestingly, when substitu-
ents were present in the ortho-position of the aryl moiety, the
spirocyclic derivatives were obtained in good to high isolated
yields (7b,e,h 69%–79%), suggesting that steric hindrance had
a negligible impact on the reaction.
To evaluate the synthetic potential of phosphonopyrrolidinones
3 for further modifications, we evaluated their reactivity as Still–
Gennari olefination partners. In the presence of paraformaldehyde,
diisopropylethylamine (DIPEA) and LiCl, phosphonopyrrolidinone 3a
afforded the corresponding 4-methylydenepyrrolidin-3-one 8a (78%
yield, Scheme 7). While the reaction of the diphenylphosphinoxy
analog was efficient with paraformaldehyde,<sup>[9]</sup> it failed to deliver

Interestingly, when tested with the fluorinated phosphinylpyrroli-
din-3-one 3a, the reaction proceeded smoothly. Using benzalde-
hyde, the corresponding product 8b was obtained in 69% yield
as a Z:E (85:15) mixture of diastereoisomers. The transformation
was further extended to other aromatic and heteroaromatic alde-
hydes, and the expected products 8b–f were obtained in low to
good yields and average to excellent diastereoselectivities. The
Z-configuration of the major diastereoisomers was determined by
(NOESY) nuclear overhauser effect spectroscopy experiments.
